## Overview

Offline embedding refresh jobs are scheduled batch processes that regenerate vector embeddings for a corpus when the underlying embedding model changes or source documents update in bulk. They provide a systematic way to maintain embedding freshness and consistency across a retrieval system without serving stale or mixed-model vectors.

## Characteristics

**Scheduling:** Typically run on a fixed cadence rather than on demand. This batching approach allows for cost-efficient bulk operations and predictable resource consumption.

**Scope:** Re-embed the full or incremental document set, depending on the trigger (model upgrade vs. document updates).

**Atomicity:** Swap the new vectors into the retrieval index atomically to avoid serving mixed-model results mid-transition. This is critical for maintaining consistent search quality and preventing confusion between old and new embeddings.

## Operational Concerns

**Model versioning:** Version the embedding model per batch. This allows tracking which embeddings were produced by which model and enables rollback or debugging if needed.

**Drift monitoring:** Monitor drift between old and new vectors to detect unexpected differences that may indicate quality regression or implementation issues.

**Staged deployment:** Stage the swap behind a blue/green index so a quality regression can be rolled back quickly without full reprocessing. The blue/green pattern ensures the system can switch between embedding versions atomically while preserving a fallback path.

## Related Concepts

- [[vector-search]] (the retrieval system being updated)
- [[blue-green-deployment]] (the deployment pattern used for index swaps)
